title: ML Kit On-device Pipelines, Lifecycle, and Privacy

scout.purpose: Master ml kit on-device pipelines, lifecycle, and privacy through a production or platform contract supported by causal evidence.
scout.realWorldUse: Specialist Android work must remain compatible, secure, measurable, accessible, distributable, and operable outside a demonstration.
scout.outcome: You can design, inspect, test, release, and defend ml kit on-device pipelines, lifecycle, and privacy.

blocks.text: ML Kit provides task-focused on-device APIs for vision, language, and generative capabilities with different availability and release maturity. Begin from a user problem, model limitations, supported devices, latency, accuracy, accessibility, and failure fallback. On-device execution can reduce network dependency and keep input local, but the SDK may still collect diagnostic or configuration data described by its disclosure documentation. Product claims and Data safety declarations must reflect the exact API and version.

blocks.text: For camera streams, own CameraX frame lifetime, orientation, crop, color format, backpressure, executor, and detector lifecycle. Process at a rate the model can sustain, close every image proxy, and discard stale results by frame identity. Confidence thresholds are product policy, not universal truth. Handle no result, multiple results, model unavailable, download pending, cancellation, rotation, backgrounding, and process recreation. Do not retain biometric or document images merely because inference is local.

blocks.caption: A focused fragment whose complete contract includes exact versions, ownership, adverse paths, compatibility, and release evidence.

blocks.text: Build an evaluation set representative of lighting, language, skin tone, device, camera, and user conditions with consent and governance. Measure latency distribution, energy, thermal behavior, memory, model load, dropped frames, and task-specific quality. Test accessibility and manual correction. Version model, preprocessing, threshold, and evaluation data together. Monitor bounded outcomes without uploading raw sensitive input. Provide clear disclosure, opt-out where appropriate, deletion, and a useful non-ML fallback.

Expert engineering makes assumptions, authority, compatibility, security, privacy, accessibility, performance, distribution, and recovery reviewable. Begin with a concrete user or platform outcome, identify trust and lifecycle boundaries, and retain exact source, dependency, toolchain, configuration, model or platform version, and artifact identity. Test realistic success plus denial, offline, process death, cancellation, corruption, version skew, resource pressure, and dependency failure. Measure representative distributions rather than best runs. Document unsupported cases, residual risk, owners, release gates, incident response, deprecation, and rollback or roll-forward. A specialised solution is production-ready only when another team can integrate, verify, operate, upgrade, disable, and remove it safely.

trap_check.mistake: Failing to close CameraX ImageProxy objects stalls the analysis pipeline even if inference itself is fast.
trap_check.why: It hides an ownership, compatibility, trust, lifecycle, or evidence gap that becomes costly outside the demonstration.
trap_check.fix: Make the disputed boundary explicit and add a representative negative or compatibility test plus operational response.

trap_check.mistake: Treating one successful device, client, model, platform build, or release as proof of the supported contract.
trap_check.why: Advanced Android ecosystems contain version, hardware, consumer, policy, and runtime variation.
trap_check.fix: Define the support matrix and verify exact artifacts across representative and adverse conditions.

challenge_intro.task: Build a lifecycle-safe text-recognition camera pipeline with backpressure, rotation, confidence policy, representative evaluation, privacy controls, and manual fallback.
challenge_intro.successLooksLike: The work includes a minimal coherent implementation, exact evidence, support and threat boundaries, adverse testing, release operation, and recovery.

recall.prompt: What four versions belong in an ML evaluation record?
recall.answer: Model, preprocessing, decision threshold or postprocessing, and the governed evaluation dataset version.

recall.prompt: What must accompany an expert Android artifact?
recall.answer: Exact source and build identity, supported versions, contracts, tests, measurements, security and privacy review, release evidence, owner, and recovery plan.
They prevent consumers and operators from treating an untested or impossible condition as a silent guarantee.
